meaning.en: Fiercely scolded, as if drenched with dog's blood.
meaning.zh: 像被狗血浇了一头，形容骂得非常凶狠。

examples.zh: 他迟到了，被老板骂得狗血淋头。
examples.en: He was late and got a severe dressing-down from his boss.

examples.zh: 考砸了，我被妈妈训得狗血淋头。
examples.en: I flunked the exam and my mother tore a strip off me.

examples.zh: 裁判判罚不公，被球迷骂得狗血淋头。
examples.en: The referee's unfair decisions earned him a torrent of abuse from fans.

usage.en: Usually passive: 被…骂得狗血淋头.

meaning.en: To move forward in step with the times.
meaning.zh: 随着时代的发展而不断前进、变化。

examples.zh: 企业要与时偕行，不断创新。
examples.en: Companies must keep pace with the times and keep innovating.

examples.zh: 教育理念也应当与时偕行。
examples.en: Educational ideas, too, should move with the times.

examples.zh: 传统文化需要与时偕行，才能焕发活力。
examples.en: Traditional culture needs to move with the times to stay vital.

usage.en: Formal; often with 与时俱进.
usage.zh: 书面语，常与“与时俱进”并用。

natural: feel as if walking on air

meaning.en: Feeling so light and happy as to seem to be turning into an immortal.
meaning.zh: 形容轻松愉快得像要成仙一样。

equivalents: feel as if floating on air

examples.zh: 喝了两杯酒，他觉得飘飘欲仙。
examples.en: After a couple of glasses of wine, he felt as if he were floating.

examples.zh: 听到这首曲子，我有种飘飘欲仙的感觉。
examples.en: Hearing the tune, I felt I was drifting among the clouds.

examples.zh: 泡完温泉，浑身飘飘欲仙。
examples.en: After the hot spring, I felt weightless.

meaning.en: Doing something secretly and furtively.
meaning.zh: 背着人做事，不想让人知道。

examples.zh: 他偷偷摸摸地溜出了教室。
examples.en: He crept furtively out of the classroom.

examples.zh: 有话就说，别这样偷偷摸摸的。
examples.en: If you have something to say, say it; don't be so sneaky.

examples.zh: 两人偷偷摸摸地谈起了恋爱。
examples.en: The two began a secret romance on the quiet.

natural: have a foot in two boats

meaning.en: To keep two options or relationships going at once, especially in love.
meaning.zh: 比喻在两个对象之间犹豫不决，或同时与两方保持关系，多指感情上不专一。

equivalents: have a foot in both camps

examples.zh: 他脚踏两只船，同时和两个女孩约会。
examples.en: He was two-timing, dating two girls at once.

examples.zh: 找工作别脚踏两只船，要尽快做决定。
examples.en: Don't hedge between two job offers; decide soon.

examples.zh: 她发现男友脚踏两只船，当即分手。
examples.en: She found her boyfriend was seeing someone else and broke up at once.

usage.en: Colloquial; 踏 may be read tà (also 脚踩两只船).

meaning.en: A single man guarding the pass is enough to hold off a host; a place of great natural strength.
meaning.zh: 一个人把守关口，成千上万的人也攻不过去，形容地势险要。

equivalents: one man can hold the pass
a stronghold that one man can defend

examples.zh: 剑门关地势险要，一夫当关，万夫莫开。
examples.en: Jianmen Pass is so steep that one man holding it could stop ten thousand.

examples.zh: 他在球门前一夫当关，连续扑出点球。
examples.en: In goal he stood like a lone gatekeeper, saving penalty after penalty.

examples.zh: 这座山口一夫当关，易守难攻。
examples.en: The mountain pass is easy to defend and hard to take.

story.en: Li Bai, 'The Road to Shu is Hard': 'One man holds the pass, ten thousand cannot break through' (一夫当关，万夫莫开).
story.zh: 李白《蜀道难》：“剑阁峥嵘而崔嵬，一夫当关，万夫莫开。”

meaning.en: In a great uproar, as noise and tumult fill the sky.
meaning.zh: 形容喧闹嘈杂，乱成一片。

examples.zh: 消息一传开，全城沸反盈天。
examples.en: When the news spread, the whole city was in an uproar.

examples.zh: 会场上吵得沸反盈天。
examples.en: The conference hall was in uproar.

examples.zh: 网络上沸反盈天，各种猜测满天飞。
examples.en: Online there was an uproar, with speculation flying everywhere.

meaning.en: Things should not be done more than three times; a warning not to push one's luck.
meaning.zh: 同样的事情不能超过三次，常用来警告不能一再重犯。

equivalents: third time lucky, fourth time never

examples.zh: 事不过三，你已经犯了两次错了。
examples.en: Three strikes and you're out; you've already made two mistakes.

examples.zh: 我可以原谅你一次、两次，但事不过三。
examples.en: I can forgive you once or twice, but not a third time.

examples.zh: 事不过三，下次再迟到就扣奖金。
examples.en: No more than three times: be late again and you lose your bonus.

meaning.en: Well organised and logical.
meaning.zh: 做事或说话有条理，次序清楚。

examples.zh: 她把房间收拾得有条有理。
examples.en: She kept her room neat and well ordered.

examples.zh: 他有条有理地向大家汇报了工作。
examples.en: He gave everyone an orderly, well-structured report.

examples.zh: 说话要有条有理，别颠三倒四。
examples.en: Speak clearly and logically; don't jumble things up.

meaning.en: Torn by both regret and remorse.
meaning.zh: 又后悔又痛恨自己。

examples.zh: 想到自己的所作所为，他悔恨交加。
examples.en: Thinking of what he'd done, he was full of remorse.

examples.zh: 她悔恨交加，彻夜未眠。
examples.en: Wracked with regret, she did not sleep all night.

examples.zh: 事故之后，司机悔恨交加。
examples.en: After the accident, the driver was consumed by guilt.

natural: show a bit of one's talent

meaning.en: To give a first modest demonstration of great ability.
meaning.zh: 有大本领的人先在小事上显一下身手。

equivalents: a first taste of one's skill

examples.zh: 这次比赛只是牛刀小试，决赛才见真章。
examples.en: This match was just a warm-up; the final will show his real worth.

examples.zh: 新人第一个项目就牛刀小试，成绩不俗。
examples.en: On his first project the newcomer showed what he could do, with good results.

examples.zh: 他在小镇上牛刀小试，便声名鹊起。
examples.en: He gave a small taste of his talent in the town and became famous.

meaning.en: Elegant and handsome, like a jade tree in the breeze (usually of a man).
meaning.zh: 像玉树迎风而立，形容男子风度潇洒、英俊挺拔。

examples.zh: 他一身西装，玉树临风。
examples.en: In his suit he looked tall, dashing and elegant.

examples.zh: 那位公子玉树临风，引人注目。
examples.en: The young gentleman, graceful as a jade tree, drew all eyes.

examples.zh: 舞台上的他玉树临风。
examples.en: On stage he cut a handsome, graceful figure.

story.en: Du Fu, 'Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup', on Cui Zongzhi: 'Fair as a jade tree before the wind' (皎如玉树临风前).
story.zh: 杜甫《饮中八仙歌》：“宗之潇洒美少年，举觞白眼望青天，皎如玉树临风前。”

usage.en: Usually of men; often jocular today.
usage.zh: 多形容男子，今多带玩笑口吻。

meaning.en: Bole judging horses; spotting talent and giving it a chance.
meaning.zh: 伯乐善于识别千里马，比喻善于发现和提拔人才。

examples.zh: 他能成才，多亏当年伯乐相马。
examples.en: He owes his success to the mentor who spotted his talent.

examples.zh: 公司要靠伯乐相马，也要靠赛场赛马。
examples.en: A company needs both talent-spotters and open competition.

examples.zh: 伯乐相马，慧眼识才，是领导的重要本领。
examples.en: Spotting talent is an essential skill for a leader.

usage.en: Often contrasted with 赛场选马 (letting talent prove itself in competition).

meaning.en: As long as one breath remains; to the last.
meaning.zh: 只要还有一口气，指到最后一刻。

examples.zh: 一息尚存，决不放弃。
examples.en: While there's breath left, I'll never give up.

examples.zh: 他一息尚存，仍坚持工作。
examples.en: With his last breath he was still working.

examples.zh: 只要一息尚存，就要为理想奋斗。
examples.en: As long as I draw breath I will fight for my ideals.

usage.en: Often in resolutions: 一息尚存，决不……

meaning.en: To stand shoulder to shoulder; also, to rank alongside.
meaning.zh: 肩并肩地站着，也比喻地位、水平相当。

examples.zh: 两位老人比肩而立，望着远方。
examples.en: The two old people stood shoulder to shoulder, gazing into the distance.

examples.zh: 他的作品已经能与大师比肩而立。
examples.en: His work can now stand on a par with the masters'.

examples.zh: 同学们比肩而立，合影留念。
examples.en: The classmates stood close together for a group photo.

natural: with a mind as calm as still water

meaning.en: Completely calm and unmoved, free of desire and agitation.
meaning.zh: 心像静止的水一样，毫无波澜，形容内心平静、不受外界干扰。

examples.zh: 经历了许多事，她早已心如止水。
examples.en: After all she's been through, she's long been unmoved.

examples.zh: 做研究需要心如止水，不被外界干扰。
examples.en: Research demands a mind undisturbed by the outside world.

examples.zh: 听到这个消息，他心如止水，没有一丝波动。
examples.en: Hearing the news, his heart was still water; nothing stirred.

usage.en: Predicate; can imply indifference or serenity.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，可指平静，也可指淡漠。

pinyin: sǐ wú zàng shēn zhī dì

meaning.en: To end up with no place even to be buried; to come to a terrible end.
meaning.zh: 死了连埋葬的地方都没有，形容下场极惨。

examples.zh: 你要是再作恶，将来会死无葬身之地。
examples.en: If you go on doing evil, you'll come to a wretched end.

examples.zh: 他发誓要让对手死无葬身之地。
examples.en: He swore to leave his rival with no place to lie in death.

examples.zh: 不听劝告，小心死无葬身之地。
examples.en: Ignore the advice and you may meet a terrible end.

meaning.en: Truly wise people do not show off and may seem foolish.
meaning.zh: 真正聪明的人不显露才智，外表看上去好像愚笨。

examples.zh: 他看似木讷，其实是大智若愚。
examples.en: He seems dull, but it's really great wisdom behind a simple air.

examples.zh: 大智若愚的人往往不爱争辩。
examples.en: Those with deep wisdom and a simple air seldom argue.

examples.zh: 这位老先生大智若愚，处事从容。
examples.en: The old gentleman, wise yet humble, handles things calmly.

meaning.en: Benevolence, righteousness and morality; now often used ironically of hypocrisy.
meaning.zh: 仁爱、正义和道德规范，今常反讽那些嘴上讲道德、实际行为恶劣的人。

examples.zh: 他满口仁义道德，背地里却干着坏事。
examples.en: He is full of talk about morality, yet does wicked things behind the scenes.

examples.zh: 教育孩子要讲仁义道德，更要以身作则。
examples.en: Teaching children about morality requires leading by example.

examples.zh: 别跟我讲什么仁义道德。
examples.en: Don't lecture me about morality.

usage.en: Often derogatory in 满口仁义道德.
usage.zh: 常说“满口仁义道德”，多含贬义。

natural: at great length and with ease

meaning.en: Writing or speech that is long, flowing and effortless.
meaning.zh: 形容文章或谈话篇幅长、气势盛、有条理。

examples.zh: 他洋洋洒洒写了几千字的评论。
examples.en: He dashed off a commentary of several thousand words.

examples.zh: 会上她洋洋洒洒讲了一个小时。
examples.en: At the meeting she spoke fluently for an hour.

examples.zh: 一篇洋洋洒洒的万言书。
examples.en: A flowing ten-thousand-word memorial.

usage.en: Usually describes writing; sometimes slightly ironic about length.
usage.zh: 多形容文章，有时略带调侃。
